meaning: Alopias, Greek alṓpēx “fox”, from the ancient vernacular “fox shark”, for its long (and therefore fox-like) tail; pelagicus, Greek pelágios “of the sea”, for living in the upper layer of the sea, in contrast to Alopias profundus (now superciliosus), which Nakamura believed dwelled on the sea bottom
description: The smallest thresher, a slim open-ocean shark with a narrow, pointed head and a small mouth. Its whip-like upper tail lobe is nearly as long as the rest of its body, and it uses it to stun small fish. The back is dark blue and the belly white, and the white does not reach up over the pectoral fin bases.
depth: Surface to about 300 m, usually in the upper 150 m
